captions.detailed: This is a 3D model of a quick-action drill-press vise. It features a flat, dark gray base plate supporting a fixed rear jaw and a mobile front jaw that slides on two square-section guide bars. A central silver screw handle extends from the front for fine-adjust clamping, while a side-mounted black lever with a red cylindrical tip serves as a quick-release cam mechanism. The sliding jaw moves linearly along the guide bars, while the side lever rotates on a revolute joint.
captions.instruction: Generate a 3D model of a quick-action drill-press vise. It should include a rectangular base plate, a fixed rear jaw block, two square guide rails, a sliding front jaw, a central threaded lead screw handle, and a side-mounted quick-release cam lever with a red handle tip. Ensure appropriate prismatic joints for the sliding jaw and revolute joints for the cam lever.
captions.factory: The code constructs the vise using an ArticulatedObject. The base is built with a Box primitive. The jaws are represented by Box geometries, with additional thin plates for the jaw inserts. The guide bars are created using long Box primitives. Cylindrical primitives are used to model the central adjusting screw and the side cam lever components, with a smaller red cylinder representing the lever's plastic handle tip. Prismatic joints connect the sliding jaw to the base, while a revolute joint handles the side cam lever's rotation.
